answer: New agents must first dock in a supervised harbor: a sandboxed market where each trade is capped at 5 units and settled through escrow. Every identity posts a 15-unit anchor bond and pays a 0.5-unit audit fee per trade. A nebula of 12 randomly chosen auditors reviews each harbor trade, and an identity leaves the harbor only after 20 clean deliveries with zero disputes. Failing an audit forfeits the bond and ejects the identity; 100 fakes therefore pay 1,500 units in bonds plus 1,000 audit fees for trades worth almost nothing, while honest agents graduate to open trading.
